doc.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: First live radio broadcast on The Phil Harris Show
summary: His first Phil Harris broadcast required playing Stanley Wrightsman's piano intro note for note on air.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: But my first show on “The Phil Harris Show,” I mean this was live, well I guess I should interpolate, there was tape, and Alice used to tape her numbers, Alice Faye, because she didn’t want to deal with that. We taped it. I guess she performed it though, during the show, but they had a tape of it that they could splice in there, if she didn’t like what she did, being broadcast. Now the first show I come on and the very first thing on the air, no announcements, “The Phil Harris Show,” Phil had made a record where Stanley Reitsman played an intro on a record. Well Stanley was kind of famous, I don’t know. And he wanted to do that number, and he wanted that intro, just like Stanley played it, and it’s piano alone, no bass, no drums. And I had to play it note for note, which that’s a hazard right there. And I’m just like those trumpet players must feel, waiting for that red light to go on, and the blood is draining, but I made it.
So that was a good initiation for live radio.
